newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Queensland says state economy to grow 4.0 pct.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Queensland says state economy to grow 4.0 pct.

text.p: Queensland's economic growth was expected to be 4.0 percent in 1996/97, slightly above forecast national economic growth of 3.5 percent, deputy premier and Treasurer Joan Sheldon said in a statement accompanying the State Budget papers.
Sheldon said the current year's forecast for growth in gross state product compared with a "serious decline" last year to only 2.2 percent, well below a projected 4.5 percent.

A major component of growth would come from a 1.5 percent increase in dwelling investment compared with a forecast national decline of three per cent and an estimated 25 percent decline in Queensland last financial year, Sheldon said.
Business investment was expected to grow by nine percent in 1996/97 against a national outlook of 14 percent, Sheldon said.
The unemployment rate was expected to remain at a year-average of about 9.3 percent but was expected to fall over the year to around nine percent by the June quarter next year, Sheldon said.
"Further reductions in the unemployment rate will be constrained by relatively strong labour force growth," Sheldon said.
